questions.q: According to this lesson, what is an Update Set fundamentally limited to, compared to real version control?
options: It's a point-in-time snapshot of a batch of changes, not a full history of every file over time
It can only contain changes to global (non-scoped) configuration
It automatically performs code review before any change is committed
It can only be used once per ServiceNow instance ever
questions.explain: An Update Set tells you what changed between opening and closing it — it was never built to track ongoing file-level history the way Git does.

questions.q: What does ServiceNow's native Source Control Integration actually connect?
options: A scoped application's files, built in Studio, to an external Git repository such as GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket
Update Sets to each other so they merge automatically
Every global platform table to a single shared spreadsheet
A user's personal profile to their GitHub account for login purposes
questions.explain: Source Control Integration links a Studio-built scoped application's actual code and configuration records to a real external Git repository.

questions.q: Which of these is a real capability Git-based source control adds that an Update Set, by itself, does not provide?
options: The ability to capture configuration changes into a batch
Branching, so multiple developers can work on separate features without colliding
The ability to preview changes before committing them to a target instance
The ability to move changes between a Dev and Test instance at all
questions.explain: Branching lets developers isolate in-progress work from each other — something a shared Update Set structurally can't do, since it's one batch, not parallel lines of development.

questions.q: Does Source Control Integration replace Update Sets everywhere on the ServiceNow platform?
options: No — it only works for the out-of-box Incident and Change tables
No — it applies to scoped applications built in Studio; Update Sets remain how most other configuration still moves between instances
Yes — Update Sets are entirely obsolete once Source Control Integration is enabled anywhere
Yes — but only for instances running on a trial license
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this isn't a platform-wide replacement — it's additive capability for Studio-built scoped applications specifically.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say source control integration matters for the chapters coming later in this course?
options: Later chapters require deleting all existing Update Sets before they can begin
Chapter 4's Automated Test Framework and Chapter 5's CI/CD concepts both assume code that can be versioned, branched, and tested in a pipeline
It's only relevant to instances that don't use Studio at all
It has no real connection to anything covered later in the course
questions.explain: Source control is the precondition for pipeline-style automation — Chapters 4 and 5 both build on application code already being trackable in a repository.
